subject: Pricing schedule redline + proposal for hard-stop tier caps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing schedule redline + proposal for hard-stop tier caps

Jordan / team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is our annotated version of the pricing schedule with two small edits we think will keep both parties comfortable while preserving throughput economics. High level: we accepted your requested tiers but asked for language that explicitly defines a hard-stop on temporary volume credits and clarifies how overage rates are calculated when the floor is breached.

Two items to call out:
- "Hard-stop" language (Section 3.2): we propose a single quarterly hard-stop cap on cumulative credits to avoid open-ended credit exposure.
- Overage calculation (Exhibit B): switched to a per-token prorated metric instead of an averaged slab to align billing and real-time metering.

Attachments: Acme_PricingSchedule_20270623_redline.pdf (redline), camila_proposed-tier-hardstop.xlsx (numeric examples).

Can you confirm Acme Legal is okay with the hard-stop mechanics? If you want, we can propose alternate wording that routes any disputed credits to a one-time reconciliation rather than an ongoing offset.

Next steps: if legal is OK, we'll circulate a clean order form for signature and pull in contracts for the DocuSign packet.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0172

From: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule redline + proposal for hard-stop tier caps

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the redline and the worked example spreadsheet. We're generally aligned with the spirit of limiting open-ended credit exposure, but a few legal questions before we sign off:

1) The proposed "quarterly hard-stop" still leaves potential ambiguity about whether credits can be carried forward as offsets in subsequent quarters; Section 3.2 should explicitly state "no carry-forward" if that's intended.
2) The overage metric in Exhibit B references "prorated per token" but lacks a precise definition of the measurement window and rounding rules. We need that to be unambiguous because our billing system runs nightly batch reconciliations.
3) We need a clause for audits: if Acme requests an audit of the usage data that leads to credits/overages, what is Redwood's obligation/cost allocation?

Also, Jordan asked whether Redwood would consider a temporary one-time onboarding credit instead of embedding a hard-stop in the long-term order form. That would simplify the contract but shift economics to an MSR/credit note.

Can you provide suggested language for "no carry-forward" and a precise definition for per-token measurement? Also indicate whether Redwood is open to adding a capped audit fee or cost-sharing arrangement.

Regards,
Tara Singh
Director, Legal — Acme Corporation
legal@acme.com

--
On Wed, Jun 23, 2027 at 9:12 AM Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jordan / team —
> 
> Thanks again for the time yesterday...

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <legal@acme.com>, Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule redline + proposal for hard-stop tier caps

Tara / Jordan —

Thanks for the clear points. Quick replies inline and attached a short clean markup with alternative wording to address the audit/carry-forward concerns.

1) No carry-forward: we can make Section 3.2 explicit: "Quarterly credits are final for the quarter in which they accrue and may not be carried forward or used to offset charges in subsequent quarters."

2) Per-token definition: Exhibit B now reads: "Per-token measurement is calculated against the number of successfully ingested and billed tokens as reported by Redwood's metering system in the nightly reconciliation window (00:00-02:00 UTC). Rounding follows standard arithmetic rounding to the nearest whole token; fractional tokens are billed at the prorated cent level as detailed in the pricing appendix."

3) Audit clause: we propose a capped audit-facility fee: Acme can request one audit per contract year; Redwood will respond within 30 days and produce billing reports. If audit finds an error >1% in Redwood's favor, Redwood absorbs the cost; if error >1% in Acme's favor, Acme reimburses the agreed audit fee (capped at $10k).

On the onboarding credit idea: Marissa and I discussed a short-term onboarding credit (one-time, 10% of first-quarter spend, applied as a credit memo) in lieu of embedding a permanent hard-stop. That preserves predictability for both sides. If you prefer the onboarding credit route, we will remove the hard-stop language and add the credit line to the order form.

I'll attach a clean order form both ways (hard-stop vs onboarding credit) so you can circulate internally.

Camila

Attachments: Acme_PricingSchedule_20270625_clean_hardstop.pdf; Acme_PricingSchedule_20270625_clean_onboard-credit.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@acme.com>, Tara Singh <legal@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing schedule redline + proposal for hard-stop tier caps

Quick internal note then external reply sent:

Camila — good approach. For deals of this size (ACME-1247), I prefer the onboarding credit instead of a hard contractual "hard-stop". The reasons:
- lower negotiation friction for procurement/legal
- keeps long-term SLAs/credits clean and auditable
- easier for finance to track as a one-time memo instead of recurring reconciliations

Karthik — please confirm the numeric impact using the workbook Camila attached and approve the 10% first-quarter credit (cap $200k) if the numbers align. If finance signs off, Camila please send updated clean order form and we'll route to DocuSign.

Jordan / Tara — thanks for working through this. We will send you the clean order form with the onboarding credit option later today. Expect DocuSign link once final sign-off completed.

Thanks,
Marissa
